name: Immerse Media Ads Tracking – Track ChatGPT Ad Conversions
author: immersemedia

sections.description:
Immerse Media Ads Tracking connects your OpenAI Ads pixel to WordPress and automatically tracks Contact Form 7 submissions as conversion events, no code required.

What’s included

  • Pixel connection (paste in your Pixel ID and you’re tracking)
  • Automatic Contact Form 7 tracking
  • Dashboard overview showing tracking status

Want to track more?

Pro is a separate, independently-sold plugin that adds:

  • Gravity Forms, WPForms, Ninja Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable Forms, and Elementor Forms tracking
  • Full WooCommerce funnel: Add to Cart, Checkout Started, Purchase (with order value, order ID, and SKUs)
  • A built-in reporting dashboard with date and integration filters

This plugin is fully functional on its own for Contact Form 7 tracking. Pro is a completely separate product, sold and hosted outside of WordPress.org.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/immerse-media-ads-tracking, or install it directly through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Immerse Media Ads Tracking > Settings and paste in your Pixel ID (found in your OpenAI Ads account under Conversions > Data Source).
  4. Toggle “Enable tracking” on and save changes.
  5. That’s it, Contact Form 7 submissions are tracked automatically.
sections.faq:
Where do I find my Pixel ID?

In your OpenAI Ads account, under Conversions > Data Source. See our step-by-step guide for details.

Does this plugin track anything besides Contact Form 7?

Not on its own. Tracking Gravity Forms, WooCommerce, and other form plugins requires Pro, a separate product.

Does this slow down my site?

No. The tracking script only loads when tracking is enabled.
sections.changelog:
1.0.10

  • Simplified “GPT Ads Tracking Pro” references to just “Pro” in the plugin description and readme.

1.0.9

  • Removed “WordPress” from the plugin name/title – WordPress.org restricts use of their own trademarked term in plugin names, separate from the earlier ChatGPT/GPT naming issue.

1.0.8

  • Renamed to “Immerse Media Ads Tracking – Track ChatGPT Ad Conversions in WordPress”. Slug changed to immerse-media-ads-tracking.

1.0.7

  • Fixed installation instructions still referencing the old plugin folder path (/gpt-ads-tracking instead of /immerse-ads-tracking).

1.0.6

  • Cleaned up remaining “GPT Ads Tracking” references throughout the readme and admin pages (headings, menu label, support links) to consistently use the plugin’s actual name.

1.0.5

  • Final naming tweak: “Immerse Ads Tracking – Track ChatGPT Ad Conversions in WordPress” for extra clarity.

1.0.4

  • Renamed plugin to “Immerse Ads Tracking – Track ChatGPT Ad Conversions” per WordPress.org’s naming guidelines, since leading with “GPT” implied an official connection to third-party technology. Slug changed to immerse-ads-tracking.

1.0.3

  • Fixed remaining namespace collisions with GPT Ads Tracking Pro: admin menu slugs, script/style enqueue handles, and the JavaScript global namespace all renamed to be unique to this plugin. Fixes duplicated admin menus and a broken license page when both plugins are active together.

1.0.2

  • Fixed a fatal error that occurred when GPT Ads Tracking Pro was active on the same site: all internal class names and constants renamed to avoid conflicting with the Pro plugin’s identically-named ones.

1.0.1

  • Replaced raw inline <script> tag with wp_register_script()/wp_add_inline_script(), per WordPress.org’s enqueue requirements.

1.0.0

  • Initial release. Contact Form 7 tracking.
